written.text: Write the precis of the following passage, giving it a suitable title:(14) The FIFA World Cup is the globe’s most prestigious football tournament, held every four years by the Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA). Uniting billions of fans and national teams, this monumental event transcends sports, serving as a powerful engine for global unity, cultural exchange, and international economic growth. Often referred to as the “beautiful Game,” football has a universal appeal that requires nothing more than a ball and an open space. The World Cup serves as the pinnacle of this sport, elevating the passion of local communities onto the international stage. Every four years, it captures the attention of a massive global audience, making it the most-watched sporting event on the planet. For participating nations, the tournament is a profound source of national pride, where everyday life pauses as communities gather to cheer for their country’s color. The tournament was first established in 1930 under the vision of then-FIFA President Jules Rimet. Since its inaugural competition in Uruguay, the event has grown exponentially in scale and competitive intensity. Over the decades, legendary teams and iconic players—such as Pelé, Diego Maradona, and Lionel Messi—have etched their names into sports history, creating enduring legacies. The event has also adapted to modern demands, integrating advanced technology like Video Assistant Referee (VAR) systems to ensure fairness and accuracy in high-stakes matches. Beyond the thrill of the matches, the World Cup carries profound socio-economic and cultural significance. It acts as a massive cultural melting pot, allowing diverse sets of fans from various backgrounds to share traditions, celebrate together, and foster mutual understanding. For the host nation, the World Cup is a massive undertaking that brings in billions of dollars through tourism, sponsorships, and media rights, while driving infrastructure development like modern stadiums and transport networks. The FIFA World Cup is more than just a month-long sporting competition; it is a global phenomenon that brings humanity together in a shared passion. Despite political and logistical challenges, its ability to unite people across borders, languages, and cultures remains unparalleled. The tournament leaves a lasting legacy by inspiring generations of young players, cementing national identities, and celebrating the sheer joy of the beautiful game.

Read the given passages carefully and answer the questions that follow. The marks for each question are indicated at the end of the question: Marketing is all about creativity and expression, so it must be an art, right? Not necessarily. While marketers once relied purely on instinct, they now rely on data-driven insights. On top of that, cutting-edge technologies and analytics have shifted the focus of marketing further toward the science side of the spectrum. Armed with so much data, marketers can now track the impact of money spent on their bottom line. In today’s world, the best approach to marketing combines both disciplines. And there’s a distinct balance to the craft—a strategic mix of interpersonal empathy and tactical analysis. Neither side of the mix can be isolated or ignored, or the results will not be encouraging. Psychologists believe the brain is separated into two distinct functions: the left-brain and the right-brain. The right side of the brain is responsible for creative thinking and artistic intuition. Series - B- 3 - As an art, marketing is all about understanding the nuances of human behaviour and determining how to make an emotional connection with the customer. More importantly, some level of art is needed to create brand standards for your company, including the logo, messaging, and overall visual identity for the brand. Right-brained marketers focus on the creative—the copy, graphics and emotions tied to the message. The science side of marketing tells us to let the data guide what strategies will be most effective. Marketers are now reporting the need for digital-first expertise, including digital proficiency, data analysis, and data science. With science, marketers adopt an outcome-centric mindset that helps them curate smarter campaigns. Over the past few years, there has been an evolving prioritisation of data-savvy talent. In 2020 and beyond, brands will need to focus on recruiting talent that can understand the complexities of AI and machine technologies. But when we reflect on earlier times, marketing was defined as the predominance of traditional advertising, like television, newspaper, and direct mail. Today, it ropes in digital channels, social media, mobile devices, and integrated, complex campaigns. And just as consumers today are more tech-savvy, employees should be able to match—and exceed—their expertise. It is important that brands continue to prioritise creative, engaging campaign messages while also focusing on key insights and performance metrics for optimal results.
